claim: The joint committee of seven deputies and seven senators (commission mixte paritaire) on France's 2027 social-security financing bill (PLFSS) fails to agree a common text on Thursday 26 November 2026.

runs.reason:
**YES is more likely.** I estimate a 90% chance that the CMP meets on Thursday, November 26, 2026, and formally concludes without a common text by 23:59 Paris time.

**Base rate.** The social-security budget is a better comparison than CMPs in general. The Senate’s November 4 report says the PLFSS 2025 committee was the first to reach agreement since the PLFSS 2011. The PLFSS 2026 committee then failed on November 26, 2025. That record strongly favors failure, though it does not measure the chance of a decision within this particular one-day window. ([senat.fr](https://www.senat.fr/rap/l26-144-1/l26-144-1_mono.html))

**What changes the odds.** The Assembly rejected the revenue section 115–1 on October 23, leaving no Assembly-amended text to reconcile with the Senate’s version. The Senate then voted to undo the suspension of the 2023 pension reform, a change the government opposed. Both facts push toward **YES**. In the other direction, Assembly rapporteur Thibault Bazin told AFP he would seek common ground, and the government signaled openness to replacing the proposed restraint on pension increases with a change to pensioners’ tax treatment. Those are possible routes to a deal, not evidence that one has been struck. ([senat.fr](https://www.senat.fr/rap/l26-144-1/l26-144-1_mono.html))

**Timing.** The Senate’s November 20 calendar lists an 08:15 start at the National Assembly, and TF1 still reported a Thursday morning meeting on November 23. The 50-day constitutional deadline expires that night. I put about 4% on postponement or no conclusion by 23:59, and about 6% on a same-day agreement. ([senat.fr](https://www.senat.fr/fileadmin/cru-1769414716/Commissions/Affaires_sociales/Fichiers/calprev_soc.pdf?utm_source=openai))

### 2. Dated Facts Moving This Case
- **Upward pressure toward failure (conditional on meeting):** On 23 October 2026, the National Assembly rejected the revenue part of the PLFSS 2027 by 115 votes to 1, causing the entire bill to be deemed rejected in first reading. Conversely, on 18 November 2026, the right- and center-dominated Senate adopted a heavily amended version of the bill by 201 votes to 124, notably repealing the suspension of the 2023 pension reform that deputies had voted for the previous year. Reporting from *Public Sénat* (18 November 2026) notes that an agreement between the two chambers in CMP is highly unlikely given these deep ideological divergences.
- **Confirming the date and preparation for failure:** On 18 November 2026, *Public Sénat* and the Ministry of Action and Public Accounts (*budget.gouv.fr*) reported that the CMP on the PLFSS 2027 is scheduled to meet on Thursday 26 November 2026 (which also marks the end of the 50-day constitutional deadline). On 20 November 2026, the convocation of the CMP was formally registered in the National Assembly's legislative dossier, and the Senate's modified text was put online as document No. 3488 on 23 November 2026. Moreover, the National Assembly's Social Affairs Committee has already cancelled a placeholder meeting for 23 November and scheduled a provisional meeting for Monday 30 November 2026 at 21:30 explicitly to examine the PLFSS 2027 in *nouvelle lecture* "in the event of failure of the joint committee".
- **Downward pressure / scheduling uncertainty:** As of 23 November 2026, legal and parliamentary trackers (*ACOMPIA*, *Max Compta*) noted that while the convocation of the CMP was registered on 20 November and the press and government calendar state it will meet on 26 November, the exact meeting time had not yet been posted on the official parliamentary agendas.

### 3. Strongest Reason the Obvious Outcome Might Fail
There are two distinct ways this claim could resolve NO. First, although *Public Sénat* and *budget.gouv.fr* state the CMP is scheduled for Thursday 26 November 2026, the official time and room notice had not yet appeared in the *Journal officiel* as of 23–24 November; if the meeting is held a day earlier (Wednesday 25 November) or postponed to Friday 27 November—or if an evening session on 26 November drags past midnight before officially recording failure—the criterion strictly resolves NO. Second, as occurred on 20 November 2026 with the end-of-year budget management bill (PLFG 2026) and in November 2024 with the PLFSS 2025, the government and the center-right bloc could strike a surprise compromise with the Senate majority in an attempt to avoid governing by ordinance or starting from scratch in a new reading.

Balancing the near-certainty of disagreement between the fragmented National Assembly and the conservative Senate against a modest (~10%) risk that the CMP meets on a different day or concludes after 23:59, and a small (~8%) chance of a surprise political deal, I estimate the probability at 0.82.

runs.reason:
The claim is likely to resolve YES: the CMP is set for the morning of 26 November, and the political gap that produced last year’s same-day failure is wider this time.

Comparable recent cases are mixed but informative. The PLFSS 2026 CMP failed on its meeting day, 26 November 2025, in well under an hour, and AFP recorded the échec that evening. The PLFSS two years earlier was conclusive, but that was under a government still trying to assemble a majority; the text was then censured. In the present hung Assembly, contested social-security CMPs fail more often than they succeed, and when they fail they are declared the same day rather than carried past midnight.

What moves this case toward failure is the size of the disagreement and the absence of a deal. The Assembly rejected the bill on 23 October 2026; the Senate, working from the original government text, adopted a rewritten version on 18 November by 201 votes to 124, restoring the 2023 pension-reform calendar and rejecting, unanimously, the de-indexation of pensions above €1,260. AFP reported on 19 November, from parliamentary and government sources, that the seven-and-seven CMP would meet on Thursday 26 November, the day the 50-day deadline expires; TF1 confirmed on 23 November that the meeting is Thursday morning and that, unlike last year, no compromise with the Socialists is on the table. The convocation itself was issued on 20 November. A morning start plus last year’s pattern of a rapid constat d’échec makes a same-day, pre-midnight record the normal path if they cannot agree.

The outcome can still miss. A bare majority inside each delegation—four senators from the Senate majority, and four deputies around the LR rapporteur and the central bloc—could adopt a common text even if the left and the RN vote against, and the government has a reason to want Senate changes locked in before any later 49.3. A postponement off the 26th, or a suspension that has not concluded by 23:59, would also be NO under the criterion as written.

A deal reached late, or a meeting suspended without a formal échec before 23:59, would also count as NO.
